rationale: E. rectale ferments acetate to butyrate via acetyl-CoA condensation. Uptaking abundant acetate (12 mmol/gDW/h) plus amino acids (2 mmol/gDW/h) for nitrogen yields 38 mmol C/gDW/h. After 13.2 mmol C/gDW/h biomass cost at μ=0.40, remaining 24.8 mmol C/gDW/h is fermented to butyrate (6 mmol/gDW/h, 24 C) and CO₂ (2.4 mmol). Nitrogen sourced from glutamine and asparagine (2 mmol/gDW/h) covers 2.8 mmol/gDW/h demand. Late stationary phase; maximize growth before nutrient crash.
